body:
I think gradient accumulation won't work with cudagraphs given that gradients will be overwritten during each iteration.

cc @eellison @BoyuanFeng

Hi, there are two options here:

- run one iteration in eager first
- set grads to None after each iteration.

We understand this is an annoyance.

Thanks for the workarounds! Better to have some path forward than none at all, so no worries about the mild inconvenience.

Any chance the error message could point to this issue in case other folks also run into this problem? I followed the recommendations in the error message (call `clone()` on the outputs, call `torch.compiler.cudagraph_mark_step_begin()` at the start of a step) and was confused why it was still failing.
Yes, I'll add something specifically for grads.

Same issue here. 
option #1 did't work.

#2 works, but I got confused here.
How does set grads to None work with gradient accumulation? If I use model.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) after each forward/backward pass, the gradients won't accumulate. 

Do you mean setting it to None only after the actual optimizer.step()? and that didn't work :(

> Hi, there are two options here:
> 
> * run one iteration in eager first
> * set grads to None after each iteration.
> 
> We understand this is an annoyance.

> Same issue here. option [#1](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/1) did't work.

The first approach worked for a toy example but not for my actual model. I didn't really have time to debug / diagnose, so I'm in the same state as you for this approach.

> [#2](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/2) works, but I got confused here. How does set grads to None work with gradient accumulation? If I use model.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) after each forward/backward pass, the gradients won't accumulate.
> 
> Do you mean setting it to None only after the actual optimizer.step()? and that didn't work :(
> 

I ended up making a copy of the gradients instead of setting them to `None` after each step:

```py
for param in model.parameters():
  if param.grad is not None:
    param.grad = param.grad.clone()
```

This approach seemed to do the right thing but was a net negative on performance in my case. It may be better for you, but we've abandoned torch.compile + CUDAGraphs until this and a few other bugs around torch.compile get resolved.

+1 

All workarounds are "fixes" that trade performance for correctness. This is quite a headache!

keep switching between +0 and clone() one after the other. +1 on dropping graphs until a proper fix is in place.... as good as guarding with compiler.is_compiling() at the end of the day

Yeah I do both unfortunately. I always warmup regardless due to overhead anyways :(

@eellison thanks for the sample code. The set-to-None approach isn't viable because we want to accumulate gradients across multiple steps.

The warmup approach worked for us on a toy model, but not on our real model. So, in principle, that's the right way forward here.

You don't actually have to run a warmup right? If you preallocate zero tensors in the gradient positions and consistently maintain their memory addresses (in the same way parameters consistently keep memory addresses), this would work too.
You can also call cudagraph_mark_step after multiple steps to work with multiple gradient accumulation: see https://gist.github.com/eellison/b121b552cc7c4912be8866563afce69a.

<details>
<summary>Repro script I used</summary>

```python
import os
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import traceback


def test_fn() -> bool:
    """Return True if NO bug. False if bug present (CUDAGraphs overwrite error).

    Reproduces issue #169545: torch.compile(mode='reduce-overhead') with
    gradient accumulation fails with
        RuntimeError: Error: accessing tensor output of CUDAGraphs that has
        been overwritten by a subsequent run.
    even when torch.compiler.cudagraph_mark_step_begin() is called at the
    start of each step and outputs are cloned.
    """
    torch._dynamo.reset()
    backend = os.environ.get("TORCH_COMPILE_BACKEND", "inductor")

    device = "cuda"
    model = nn.Linear(10, 1).to(device)
    # mode='reduce-overhead' enables CUDAGraphs in the inductor path.
    compiled_model = torch.compile(
        model, fullgraph=True, backend=backend, mode="reduce-overhead"
    )

    try:
        for _ in range(5):
            torch.compiler.cudagraph_mark_step_begin()
            input = torch.randn(
                (10,), dtype=torch.float32, requires_grad=True, device=device
            )
            outputs = compiled_model(input).clone()
            loss = outputs.sum().clone()
            loss.backward()
    except RuntimeError as e:
        if "accessing tensor output of CUDAGraphs that has been overwritten" in str(e):
            return False  # Bug reproduced
        raise  # Different error - let it propagate

    return True  # No bug


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(f"torch.__version__ = {torch.__version__}")
    print(f"CUDA available: {torch.cuda.is_available()}")
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        print(f"GPU: {torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)}")

    try:
        ok = test_fn()
    except Exception:
        traceback.print_exc()
        os._exit(2)

    if ok:
        print("PASSED: gradient accumulation works with CUDAGraphs")
        os._exit(0)
    else:
        print(
            "FAILED: Bug reproduced - CUDAGraphs overwrite error during gradient accumulation"
        )
        os._exit(1)

```
